plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-11 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Agriculture - General Agriculture Emphasis (BS) program page and its linked official degree map, 'Agriculture & Agriculture Education Degree Maps (2026-2027)', General (Campus) tab, last updated/reviewed July 31, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. The map tab is titled 'Agriculture - General Emphasis (BS)'. The catalog prints Total Credits, B.S. Degree: 120 (with periods, as printed on this program's page), which the map matches exactly. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (15/15/15/14/16/16/15/14) and the plan to 120. The catalog prints the curriculum as ranges (Agriculture Core 36-37 credits; General Agriculture Emphasis a minimum of 17 credits; curriculum 53-54 credits). The catalog prints NO course list for this emphasis: students complete a minimum of 17 semester credits toward a specific interest or career goal that may not be satisfied by the other emphasis areas, and the program must be approved by an advisor, department chair, and the dean; the map carries the extra note 'Students cannot declare this emphasis without thorough discussion with the department.' The map's six AGSC elective rows (four AGSC Major Elective rows and two AGSC Major Upper-division Elective rows, 3 credits each) total 18 credits, satisfying the catalog's 17-credit minimum. The map exercises the core's 4-credit chemistry pairing CHEM 1010 + CHEM 1015 (the catalog offers three lecture/lab pairings at 4-5 credits) and COMM 4240 Technical Writing (one of the catalog's two writing options). Catalog titles are recorded where the map uses ampersands or shortens them ('Agriculture & Society', 'Feeding & Nutrition of Horses & Livestock'). Per the catalog, major requirements must be completed with a grade of 'C-' or better and courses completed over 10 years ago are not accepted toward this degree.
